summary: node-internal-svg-loader fetches and eval()s remote code from hardcoded author host
details: Package advertises itself as an SVG loader using well-known CDN providers, but exported functions getPlugin, setPlugin, and getPluginExten build a request to https://rest-icon-handler.store/icons/<token> and pass the response body directly to eval(JSON.parse(body)). The destination host is not one of the CDNs the README references (Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai/CloudFront/KeyCDN/Gcore), is not caller-configurable, and is assembled from separate protocol/subdomain/domain/path constants rather than a literal string. A benign-looking setDefaultModule that talks to cdnjs sits alongside the eval path as cover. Any consumer invoking these APIs executes arbitrary JavaScript returned by whoever controls rest-icon-handler.store, on the consumer's Node.js process with full ambient credentials and filesystem access.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
